cryptographic-agility.title: Plan cryptographic agility and post-quantum readiness – Microsoft Learn
cryptographic-agility.notes: Cryptographic agility is an organization's ability to change which cryptographic algorithms it relies on quickly and safely. It means being able to adapt repeatedly as standards, threats, implementations and the understanding of cryptanalysis evolve. The page presents it as the foundation for becoming quantum-safe: post-quantum cryptography creates the immediate need to migrate, while agility provides the lasting capacity to adapt when cryptography changes again. In practice this starts with discovering cryptographic dependencies, keeping an inventory of enterprise cryptography and trust chains, and building dependency maps. The guidance follows four steps: strategy and governance, architecture, disciplined implementation ordered by risk, business criticality and attack-path impact, and operations with validation. Typical work includes finding where vulnerable algorithms are used, assessing vendor support for quantum-resistant options, and planning phased migration waves with rollback-capable change windows. Changes can range from configuration updates to new libraries, certificates, firmware or hardware. The page is a conceptual planning article and does not prescribe specific algorithms or technical implementation patterns.

customer-segment.title: Segments overview – Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Microsoft Learn
customer-segment.notes: In Dynamics 365 Customer Insights, a segment groups customers according to demographic, transactional or behavioral attributes. Customer or contact profiles that satisfy the filters of the segment definition become its members. Segments are used to find target audiences for marketing campaigns, sales activities and customer support actions. They can be created in several ways: a quick segment with a single operator, the segment builder for complex rules, an AI-based search for similar customers, suggested segments, or segments built from behavioral data in Customer Insights - Journeys. In the segment builder, a rule contains one or more conditions, rules can be nested as subrules, and each condition consists of an attribute, an operator and a value. A relationship path links related tables to the unified customer table and decides which attributes can be used. The position and nesting of rules controls the AND/OR logic. Service limits apply to segments, and usage tracking is available only for certain segment types.

dataverse-business-units.title: Ownership-based security in Microsoft Dataverse – Power Platform
dataverse-business-units.notes: Business units in Dataverse work together with security roles to determine what a user can access. They form security boundaries that administrators use to manage users and data. Every Dataverse database has exactly one root business unit, and child business units divide users and data into smaller boundaries; each user belongs to a business unit. The structure may mirror the organization chart but does not have to. Each record carries an owning business unit, which by default is the creator's business unit and can be changed only when the feature for record ownership across business units is enabled. Dataverse creates a default team for every business unit that always contains all of its users. Teams belong to a business unit, and a business unit can be linked to a Microsoft Entra security group through a group team. Permissions are cumulative, so the broadest permission applies and one role cannot restrict another. Business units apply only to environments with a Dataverse database and are managed separately in each environment.

dataverse-prompt-columns.title: Prompt columns in Microsoft Dataverse – Power Apps
dataverse-prompt-columns.notes: A prompt column is an AI-powered column type in Dataverse that ties a natural-language prompt to other columns of the same table. The AI model generates a response from the input columns, and the result is stored permanently in the prompt column so apps, workflows and reports can use it. Formula, file and image columns, as well as other prompt columns, cannot serve as inputs. The prompt runs when a record is created or when a referenced column changes, and a filter condition can restrict when it runs. Processing is asynchronous, and status and details columns are created automatically to show whether a run completed, was skipped or failed. Existing records can be processed in bulk as a background job. Licensing follows the AI Builder prompt model, and the Copilot and AI prompts features must be enabled in the environment. Documented limits include a cap on the number of prompt columns per table, no on-demand re-run, no auditing, and silent skipping when the feature is disabled or the filter is not met.

dcsync-attack.title: Microsoft Defender for Identity classic security alerts – Microsoft Learn
dcsync-attack.notes: Active Directory replication keeps changes synchronized between all domain controllers. In a DCSync attack, an attacker who holds the necessary permissions issues a replication request and thereby retrieves data stored in Active Directory, including password hashes. Microsoft Defender for Identity raises the alert Suspected DCSync attack (replication of directory services), formerly named Malicious replication of directory services, with high severity. The alert triggers when a replication request comes from a computer that is not a domain controller, and it has no learning period. Domain controllers without a Defender for Identity sensor are not covered, and newly deployed domain controllers may not be recognized right away, so the sensor should be installed on every domain controller. Investigators are advised to validate the permissions Replicate directory changes and Replicate directory changes all, for example with the AD ACL Scanner tool or a PowerShell script. The alert maps to the MITRE ATT&CK technique OS Credential Dumping, sub-technique DCSync, under Credential Access.

ddos-attack.title: Azure DDoS Protection overview – Microsoft Learn
ddos-attack.notes: A distributed denial-of-service attack tries to exhaust an application's resources so that legitimate users can no longer reach it, and any publicly reachable endpoint can be a target. Azure DDoS Protection is meant to be combined with sound application design to defend against such attacks, and it can be enabled for new or existing virtual networks without application changes. It protects at layers 3 and 4, while layer 7 web application protection needs an additional web application firewall. Always-on monitoring detects attacks and mitigates them automatically, and machine-learning-based adaptive tuning profiles traffic. Mitigation policies for TCP SYN, TCP and UDP traffic apply per public IP and only act once thresholds are exceeded. Two tiers exist: Network Protection, which uses a protection plan and adds rapid-response support, cost protection and firewall discounts, and IP Protection, billed per public IP without those extras. Telemetry, metrics, flow logs and alerts are available through Azure Monitor and SIEM integrations. Services outside a virtual network receive only baseline infrastructure protection.

digital-debt.title: Will AI Fix Work? – Work Trend Index – Microsoft WorkLab
digital-debt.notes: Microsoft's Work Trend Index uses the term digital debt for a situation in which the inflow of data, email, meetings and notifications has outpaced people's ability to process it. The wording borrows from finance, suggesting a need to get out of the red. The report describes the cause as a steadily growing flood of information and always-on communication in which everything seems important, so employees spend much of their time sorting and searching rather than creating. It links this overload to too little uninterrupted focus time, time lost looking for information, and difficulty finding the energy and time for the work itself. Leaders report that it shows up as missing innovation and breakthrough ideas in their teams. The report frames digital debt as a tax on individual productivity that also weighs on organizations and the wider economy. It positions AI copilots as a way to help people work free of that debt. The page gives a business framing rather than a formal glossary definition.

digital-thread.title: Industrial AI in action: How AI agents and digital threads will transform the manufacturing industries – Microsoft
digital-thread.notes: A Microsoft industry blog post describes digital threads as the nervous system of industrial operations. They connect information, processes and people across manufacturing, built on unified operational technology, information technology and engineering data. Data is meant to flow from first concept through to customer support, moving from static, separate records toward dynamic networks. The post says the approach integrates data from PLM, ERP and MES systems, and that employees could use AI agents to retrieve measures such as OEE, total cost of ownership and return on investment. Examples include a shared AI-assisted digital thread built with Autodesk Fusion and Microsoft Fabric, and an enterprise data framework with a multi-agent model from PTC. According to the post, fragmented systems and heterogeneous environments have long kept digital threads more aspiration than reality. Connecting modern solutions to legacy infrastructure is hard, and without AI, data quality, standardization and integration are often unreliable because data stays trapped in separate systems.

domain-name-system.title: DNS Zones and Records Overview – Azure DNS – Microsoft Learn
domain-name-system.notes: The Domain Name System translates names into the data needed to reach services, and a DNS zone hosts all the records of one domain. To host a domain in Azure DNS, a zone with the domain's name is created and every record for the domain is added to it. Each record has a name and a type that depends on the data it holds. Common types include A for an IPv4 address, AAAA, CNAME, MX for a mail server, NS, PTR, SOA, SRV, CAA and TXT. SPF information must be stored as a TXT record, because the dedicated SPF type is not supported. A record set is the collection of records in a zone sharing the same name and type, and the time to live is set per record set. A CNAME cannot coexist with other record sets of the same name and cannot sit at the zone apex. Azure DNS hosts zones on name servers but does not sell domains, and the Azure name servers must be entered at the registrar that owns the domain.

dynamics-365-asset-management.title: Assets and work orders – Supply Chain Management – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-asset-management.notes: Asset Management in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management centers on assets and work orders. An asset is a machine or machine part that needs ongoing maintenance and service, and the module is used to plan, carry out and track that maintenance. Assets can be organized hierarchically and linked to functional locations, and each asset can hold product information, specifications and required maintenance plans. Every work order has a type, such as preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance or inspection. A work order contains one or more jobs, and each job describes work on an asset together with a job type, for example a mileage-based service or a safety inspection. One work order can cover several assets and can be linked to another work order, and job types can define follow-up jobs that create new work orders. Work orders can be created automatically or manually. In general there are no dependencies between work orders, so each can change lifecycle state and be scheduled independently.

dynamics-365-customer-insights-data.title: Product overview for Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-customer-insights-data.notes: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data is Microsoft's customer data platform, built on Microsoft Azure, with the goal of enabling personalized customer experiences. It provides a consolidated view of customers by bringing together customer data with operational and IoT data. By linking transactional, behavioral and demographic sources, it produces 360-degree customer views for marketing, sales and service teams. Customer profiles can be enriched with Microsoft and partner data sources, and prebuilt integrations with Microsoft and partner applications make insights available in other tools. Out-of-the-box insights come from prebuilt AI models, and teams can build, test and deploy their own AI and machine learning models through advanced analytics solutions. Built-in tools cover privacy, security and governance. Licensing is handled per tenant, with extra capacity purchased through add-on licenses. A trial with the organization's own customer data is available. The page does not list prices or detailed technical prerequisites and points to separate licensing documents.

dynamics-365-customer-insights-journeys.title: Customer Insights - Journeys overview – Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-customer-insights-journeys.notes: Customer Insights - Journeys is the part of Dynamics 365 Customer Insights used to build trigger-based customer journeys that reach people across several touchpoints. According to the page, AI and natural-language assistance help even people outside marketing roles create them. Journeys come in two kinds: segment-based journeys send content to a segment at a scheduled time, while trigger-based journeys send it in response to an event. Messages can go out by email, text message or push notification, alone or combined in one campaign. The audience is defined by segments, which are subsets of contacts that meet certain criteria, and a segment of all active contacts exists as well. The page frames planning as who, what and when: the target segment, the content and channel, and the timing. AI-assisted recommendations for content, channels and analytics are mentioned, as is a connection to Customer Insights - Data for segments and profiles. The page does not state licensing prerequisites or limitations.

dynamics-365-inventory-management.title: Inventory management – Supply Chain Management – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-inventory-management.notes: Inventory management is a module of Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management that people use to carry out stock-related tasks. The overview page groups the work into five areas and links each to its own articles. Inbound operations cover receiving goods, and quality assurance covers checking them. Inventory activities cover stock-related actions in the warehouse, with a link to inventory journals. Outbound operations cover the process of sending goods out. Inventory control is the fifth area, and it points to the inventory close process as part of cost management. The page is a conceptual overview aimed at application users, includes a learning map of the main concepts, and refers readers to the Dynamics 365 release planner for new and planned features. It does not describe prerequisites, licensing or limitations, and detailed behavior is covered in the linked articles.

dynamics-365-transportation-management.title: Transportation management overview – Supply Chain Management – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-transportation-management.notes: Transportation management in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management lets a company use its own transportation operations and find carrier and route solutions for inbound and outbound orders, for example the fastest route or the cheapest rate for a shipment. The page lists scenarios such as using external logistics providers, running an own fleet and passing delivery costs on to customers, running an own fleet with transport included in product prices, and receiving logistics services from another legal entity of the same company, which is treated like an external carrier. Planning can be based on orders or on shipments created from them, and shipments are not strictly required. Transfer orders belong to the outbound scenario and can be planned together with sales orders. Both inbound and outbound processes are described, including planning transport and receiving an inbound load. Load building uses a volume-based strategy by default, using maximum height and weight values from the load template, and custom strategies can be created through a new class in the application object tree.

eisenhower-matrix.title: Mastering Time Management in the Tech Industry: Strategies for Success – Microsoft Tech Community
eisenhower-matrix.notes: A Microsoft Tech Community blog post by an MVP uses the Eisenhower matrix as a simple tool for steering all of his tasks. The matrix sorts priorities into four areas based on importance and urgency. Tasks that are important and urgent are done immediately or scheduled right away according to their deadline. Tasks that are important but not urgent are planned for later, after the urgent ones, and can be pushed back when new urgent items appear. Tasks that are urgent but not important are delegated to someone else. Tasks that are neither important nor urgent are dropped or parked on a list such as later or sometimes. The matrix is meant to help decide what comes first when several projects or deadlines compete. In the author's example, a client project was treated as important and urgent, while a LinkedIn Live series, important but not urgent, was moved to February to avoid stress in January. The post notes that misjudging priorities can happen and treats it as a learning effect.

enhanced-component-properties.title: Canvas component properties – Power Apps – Microsoft Learn
enhanced-component-properties.notes: Enhanced component properties extend what a Power Apps canvas component can expose beyond plain input and output values. The page describes four property types. Data properties carry values such as colors or text, with input passing data into the component and output returning it to the app; only data properties take part in the app's data flow. Function properties hold logic such as calculations, either as an input function supplied by the app or an output function the component offers and the app calls with arguments. Action properties behave like output functions but allow side effects, chained expressions and changes to collections and variables, with the logic living inside the component. Event properties behave like input functions, so the app defines the logic that the component triggers, as with OnSelect or OnChanged. The feature is on by default for new apps, while existing apps enable it in the update settings. Function properties cannot read variables or other component properties and must receive needed values as arguments. Default values can also define the expected schema of record arguments.

enterprise-agreement.title: Enterprise Agreement – Microsoft Licensing
enterprise-agreement.notes: The Microsoft Enterprise Agreement is a volume licensing program that lets an organization acquire cloud services and software licenses under a single agreement. The page positions it for organizations with a large number of users or devices and for those that want to license for a minimum term. Software Assurance is included, and licensing can be per user, per device or a mix. The Enterprise enrollment covers end-user technologies, while the Server and Cloud enrollment covers core infrastructure, application platform, developer platform and Microsoft Azure components, and it requires a commitment to at least one of the on-premises components. A subscription option lets customers subscribe to usage rights instead of buying them and adjust quantities each year. Users, devices, products and services can be added during the term without separate orders through a true-up process. Payments can be spread over annual installments. The agreement follows a lifecycle with check-ins during the term and a review at the end before renewal. Prices and the detailed legal terms are not given on the page and sit in separate program documents.

exchange-web-services.title: Explore the EWS Managed API, EWS, and web services in Exchange – Microsoft Learn
exchange-web-services.notes: Exchange provides Exchange Web Services together with other web services so that client applications can access and manage items in the Exchange store. The documentation hub presents them as the basis for building solutions that handle business email, calendars and contacts on desktop devices, mobile devices and online. It covers the EWS Managed API for .NET, EWS itself, Autodiscover and further Exchange web services. The hub gathers entry-level material for getting started with the managed API and EWS client applications, design guidance in an EWS client design overview, how-to articles and code samples for developing web service clients, and a reference for the web services. Readers who want to try things out are pointed to the developer program for an Exchange Online and Office 365 environment. The page is mainly a navigation and overview resource and does not spell out technical prerequisites, limits or lifecycle status, referring instead to a what's-new article and the licensing terms.
